title: Every confirmed unpinned source carries a detection baseline after phase 3, so a live page without a date is decided by its text hash at the next census
goal: census.py confirm (phase 3) writes, for each confirmed unpinned source that has none, the detection baseline factdiff.py detect reads (the provider's ETag or Last-Modified, version id, or the hash of the normalized text from the document phase 2 or factdiff fetched), never a baseline from a text no one compared; census.py check with --factdiff then takes factdiff's unchanged verdict for a live page with no last-updated date instead of bucket NEEDS-READING; a new command or flag lists the live unpinned sources with no baseline (count by host, exit 1 when any) so the gap is visible before a census starts. The 2026-09-26 census sent about 200 live pages to reading for having no date, and most came back confirmed unchanged.
notes: Premise from kb/public/_census/2026-09-26.csv (tally run 2026-10-10): NEEDS-READING rows with evidence 'HTTP 200, no last-updated date' (with or without a redirect note) number about 205; phase 2 recorded about 163 of them confirmed, 36 updated, 10 superseded. On 2026-10-10, of 2990 live sources in kb/public/_sources.csv, 461 have no row in _fetch_state.csv (206 raw.githubusercontent.com pins, which need none; 94 learn.microsoft.com, 53 gitlab.com, the rest a long tail) and 58 have a row with no ETag, Last-Modified, version id or text hash (techcommunity.microsoft.com 14). The listing command the goal names makes that count a tool output instead of a one-off script.
